People exact has more slack. - **Comparing neighbours makes a 1-frame first stage work.** If a second's one-frame answer differs from the next or previous second's, something is changing there, so look closer. ### The chosen rule: `staged-1>3>all-VPN` (D-017) ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Second with n frames"] --> B["Stage 1: run the middle frame"] B --> C{"N: differs from the previous or next second's stage-1 result?"} C -- "no" --> W["Write the second from the frames run"] C -- "yes, and n > 1" --> D["Stage 2: add 3 evenly spaced frames"] D --> E{"V: frames disagree on an object? or P: on the person count?"} E -- "no" --> W E -- "yes" --> F["Stage 3: run every frame of the second"] F --> W ``` - The positions nest: the middle frame is one of the three stage-2 frames, so no frame is ever run twice. - The second's answer uses **every frame that was run** for it, with the brief's half-vote and median rules. - Rule N needs one second of look-ahead, so `run.py` buffers decoded frames. They're kept compact, in their decoded form, and only frames sent to the model are converted to BGR. ### Results The real `run.py` output equalled the simulator's prediction on **all 27,388 dev seconds**, and the number of frames run matched for every video. | Measure | Dev | Holdout | |---|---|---| | F1 | 0.9947 | 0.9947 | | People exact | 0.9940 | 0.9950 | | Within ±1 | 0.9999 | 0.9999 | - **Speed:** **1,049 s**, against 3,833 s for the baseline: **3.65× faster** (S-3). - **Frames run:** 24.0%. The speed-up is smaller than 1/0.24 ≈ 4.2× because every frame is still decoded, batches are smaller, and there is more Python work per second, all on one CPU core. This result is approximate by design: the output no longer equals the every-frame reference exactly, but it passes the brief's thresholds and our stricter margins with room to spare. The sampling rule was then frozen; later steps only changed how fast the same rule runs. ### Memory safety (D-019) Buffering seconds for the look-ahead raised a memory question. A check found and fixed four problems: - **A single huge second could be buffered whole.** Now a second over 512 MB is run frame by frame as it's decoded, still using every frame. This never happens on real data. - **The out-of-memory retry kept the failed batch alive.** It ran inside the `except` block. It now retries outside it, after releasing memory, so the failed batch can be freed. - **Ultralytics kept the last batch's images between calls.** These are now dropped after every call. - **After an out-of-memory error, batches went straight back to full size.** The batch size is now halved and remembered per image shape. Tests with real 4K video confirmed that memory stays bounded and that out-of-memory recovery works. ## 5. Step 0: profiling, to find where the time goes With sampling fixed, we profiled every stage (D-021; 10-video profiling set, FP32): | Stage | Share of wall time | |---|---| | **Model forward pass (FP32)** | **75.6%** | | Decode (PyAV) | 9.4% | | Convert YUV → BGR (frames that are run) | 7.8% | | Preprocess (letterbox, copy to GPU) | 3.1% | | Postprocess (NMS, results) | 2.7% | | Sampling, aggregation, writing | 1.3% | The conclusion: the forward pass dominates, so precision and the inference engine are the main levers. The CPU stages, about 24% of the time, run one after another with the GPU work, so overlapping them was the next lever. ## 6. The optimisation steps Each step was screened on the 10-video profiling set. If it was promising, it was timed in full on the 66-video set, interleaved with a control run (control, candidate, control, candidate), and then put through all the correctness checks. ```mermaid flowchart LR S1["Baseline: every frame, FP32
3,833 s"] --> S3["+ staged sampling
1,049 s"] S3 --> S6["+ FP16
658 s"] S6 --> S7["+ decode in a separate thread
534 s"] S7 --> S10["+ TensorRT FP16
310 s"] ``` All times are measured, on the same 66 videos (5.21 h of video) and the same GPU 0 (a Quadro RTX 6000). ### 6.1 FP16 inference (D-022): promoted - **Change:** run the PyTorch model in half precision (`quantize=16`). - **Why it helps:** the forward pass was 76% of the time. FP16 moves half the data and uses the GPU's tensor cores. The forward pass got 1.84× faster. - **Correctness:** frame by frame, the detected object set changed on 0.070% of dev frames, almost all of them detections with confidence between 0.40 and 0.45, right at the threshold. | | Dev | Holdout | |---|---|---| | F1 | 0.9938 | 0.9947 | | People exact | 0.9928 | 0.9939 | | Within ±1 | 0.9999 | 0.9999 | - **A subtlety:** FP16 results depend slightly on which frames share a batch. Confidences moved by up to 0.007, against under 0.0005 in FP32. This explained why one frame per video differed from the simulation in 4 of 101 dev videos. Each difference was traced to a specific frame. - **Speed:** **658 s**, from 1,049 s (**−37%**, S-6). ### 6.2 Decode in a separate thread (D-023): promoted - **Change:** a decoder thread reads and decodes videos and passes the frames, in order, through a queue limited to 512 MB. The main thread runs the same sampling, inference and writing code as before. - **Why it helps:** after FP16, the CPU stages were about 37% of the time, and they ran while the GPU waited. PyAV releases Python's global interpreter lock (GIL) while decoding, so decoding really runs in parallel with GPU work. ```mermaid flowchart LR P["Parquet rows"] --> D["Decoder thread
PyAV decode, exact timestamps"] D --> Q["Queue
at most 512 MB of frames, in order"] Q --> M["Main thread
staged sampling: choose frames"] M --> G["GPU: YOLO11l batches
of up to 32 same-size frames"] G --> M M --> O["Writer
one JSON line per second"] ``` - **Stricter rules for this step:** concurrency bugs can drop or reorder frames silently. So this step had to produce **byte-identical output and exactly the same frames sent to the model** as the FP16 version, and it did, on every set. - **Testing:** unit tests run it against the serial version with tiny queues that force constant waiting, and with decoder failures. A crash in the decoder thread ends the run instead of hanging it. - **Fallback:** the serial loop is kept as `--pipeline serial`. - **Speed:** **534 s**, from 658 s (**−19%**, S-7). ### 6.3 PyAV decoder threading (D-024): rejected - **Idea:** let FFmpeg use several threads per video. Measured alone, decoding got about 4.9× faster. - **Result:** no end-to-end gain. All configurations were within ±0.6% of the control. - **Why:** after step 6.2, decoding was already hidden in its own thread, and it had about 4× more throughput than the pipeline used. The limit was the main thread, so faster decoding only filled the queue sooner. The option was removed to keep `run.py` simple. ### 6.4 TensorRT FP16 (D-025): promoted - **Change:** run YOLO11l as a **TensorRT engine**. TensorRT is NVIDIA's inference compiler: it turns the network into an engine optimised for one specific GPU model. The engine is built with Ultralytics' export (FP16, dynamic batch 1–32, image size 640). Letterbox and NMS stay exactly as in PyTorch. - **Why it helps:** even in FP16 PyTorch, the forward pass was still the largest stage. - **Correctness:** the object set changed on 0.123% of dev frames, about twice FP16's rate, again at the threshold. | | Dev | Holdout | |---|---|---| | F1 | 0.9928 | 0.9933 | | People exact | 0.9922 | 0.9934 | | Within ±1 | 0.9998 | 0.9999 | - **No batch dependence:** unlike PyTorch FP16, TensorRT gives the same result whether a frame runs alone or in a batch. So the simulation predicted the real run exactly, with 0 differing seconds on both sets. - **Speed:** **310 s**, from 534 s (**−42%**, S-10). The two runs were byte-identical. - **Memory:** TensorRT reserves 4.6 GB of GPU memory up front, and peak RAM fell from 7.9 to 6.2 GB. ### 6.5 Deferred and not applicable (D-026) - **#5 batch-size tuning:** deferred. In FP32, going from batch 32 to 64 gained under 1%. - **#6 less preprocessing and copying:** deferred. - **#7 cuDNN benchmark mode and `torch.compile`:** don't apply to the TensorRT path. Both deferred steps were left until the full results were secured, because each would have required re-running the whole validation. ## 7. Summary of measured speed and accuracy | Version | Wall time (66 videos) | Speed-up vs baseline | Dev F1 / exact / ±1 | Holdout F1 / exact / ±1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | Baseline, every frame, FP32 (S-1) | 3,833 s | 1.0× | 1.0000 / 1.0000 / 1.0000 | — | | + staged sampling (S-3) | 1,049 s | 3.65× | 0.9947 / 0.9940 / 0.9999 | 0.9947 / 0.9950 / 0.9999 | | + FP16 (S-6) | 658 s | 5.8× | 0.9938 / 0.9928 / 0.9999 | 0.9947 / 0.9939 / 0.9999 | | + threaded decoding (S-7) | 534 s | 7.2× | same as FP16 (byte-identical output) | same as FP16 | | **+ TensorRT FP16 (S-10, final)** | **310 s** | **12.4×** | **0.9928 / 0.9922 / 0.9998** | **0.9933 / 0.9934 / 0.9999** | Every row is a measurement except the baseline's holdout cell, which wasn't measured. All scores are measured against the every-frame FP32 reference. Each optimisation gave up a little accuracy for speed, and every version stays well above the brief's thresholds (0.95 / 0.85 / 0.95) and our own margins (0.99 / 0.98 / 0.995). **Full run (S-11, measured):** - **Content:** all 50 files: 1,650 videos, 461,757 seconds, about 128 h of video. - **Time:** **1 h 57 min 38 s** on one Quadro RTX 6000. The baseline estimate was about 25.5 h. - **Problems:** 0 errors. - **Completeness:** an independent checker (`validation/check_full_results.py`) works out the expected seconds from the videos' packet timestamps without using `run.py`. Every video and second was present. **Estimate for the graders' 13 h test set:** about 12 minutes on the RTX 6000 at the S-11 rate. The RTX 4090 is a different GPU (Ada, not Turing), so its time has to be measured, not assumed. ## 8. Deployment on the grading machine ```mermaid flowchart TD I["pip install -r requirements.txt
exact versions, about 9 GB of wheels"] --> P["python prep.py
untimed, online"] P --> P1["Download yolo11l.pt and check its sha256"] P1 --> P2["Build weights/yolo11l.engine for this GPU"] P2 --> P3["Check the engine runs a batch of 32"] P3 --> R["python run.py --input ... --output ...
timed, offline"] R --> E{"Engine present and loads?"} E -- "yes" --> T["TensorRT FP16"] E -- "no" --> F["Warning on stderr, then PyTorch FP16 fallback"] ``` - **The engine is built on the grading machine.** A TensorRT engine only runs on the GPU model and TensorRT version it was built with, so it can't be shipped prebuilt. `prep.py` builds it during the untimed preparation step. That took about 6 minutes here, after a 4 GB TensorRT download during `pip install`. - **Fallback:** if the engine is missing or doesn't load, `run.py` prints a warning and runs PyTorch FP16, which is slower but validated (section 6.1). - **Offline:** `run.py` sets `YOLO_OFFLINE=1` and turns off Ultralytics' auto-install. Under `validation/offline_guard.py`, which blocks Python networking, the run made 0 network attempts. - **Clean-environment test (D-027):** - Setup: a fresh venv and a fresh copy of the repository, then `prep.py`, then offline runs on dev and the holdout. - Scores with the newly built engine: dev F1 0.9918, people exact 0.9920, within ±1 0.9998; holdout 0.9935 / 0.9933 / 0.9999. All 17 fixtures and 23 unit tests passed. - **Engines vary between builds:** TensorRT can choose different kernels each time it builds, so two builds aren't bit-identical. The new engine changed 0.12% of seconds. With the original engine, the clean environment reproduced S-10 and `results.jsonl.gz` byte for byte, so the difference comes only from the rebuild. A run on the grading machine will differ from `results.jsonl.gz` by about this much. ## 9. What we would look at next - **The main thread is now the limit:** converting frames to BGR, plus pre- and post-processing, still run between GPU batches. Experiment #6 (less preprocessing and copying) targets this. - **Batch size (#5):** a small expected gain. - **A faster sampling rule** (`staged-1>3>9>all-VN`, 15.8% of frames) is documented in D-016 but not implemented. It gives up people-count accuracy (exact about 0.966) for speed, and would only be worth it if speed ever became critical.

"""Video indexing: staged sampling (D-017), TensorRT FP16 (D-025), threaded decoding (D-023), one GPU.

    python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl

For every second of every video, the output records which of five objects
(person, car, dog, laptop, cell phone) are present and how many people are visible,
using YOLO11l. The rules are in brief §§3–5. Each design choice is labelled with its
DECISIONS.md entry.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import io
import json
import math
import os
import statistics
import sys
import time
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path

# The timed run is offline (brief §6): Ultralytics must not try the network or install packages.
# Neither setting changes any computation (D-025).
os.environ.setdefault("YOLO_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("YOLO_AUTOINSTALL", "false")

TARGETS = ["person", "car", "dog", "laptop", "cell phone"]  # brief §1, output order
PERSON = 0
PREDICT_KW = dict(imgsz=640, conf=0.4, iou=0.7, verbose=False)  # iou must be explicit (D-014)
MAX_BATCH_FRAMES = 32                 # D-015 C2
MAX_BATCH_BYTES = 1 << 30             # D-015 C5: limit by bytes, about 1 GB of BGR frames
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


class VideoError(Exception):
    """A per-video failure: write one error line and continue with the next video."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- output

class Writer:
    """The only writer of the output file (D-015 C1)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.f = open(path, "w", buffering=1 << 20)
        self.n_seconds = self.n_errors = 0

    def second(self, video: str, s: int, objects: list[str], people: int):
        self.f.write(json.dumps({"video": video, "second": s, "objects": objects,
                                 "people": people}) + "\n")
        self.n_seconds += 1

    def error(self, video: str, msg: str):

def _predict(self, imgs):
        """One predict call on same-shape images (D-015 C2)."""

        """For each image: (which targets are present, person count).

          - the retry happens only after leaving the `except` block, so the exception's

          - an OOM on a single frame is a VideoError for this video only.

        out, i = [], 0

def process_video_staged(video: str, mp4, det, w: Writer, keep_partial: bool, stages, flags,
                         frames=None) -> int:
    """Staged sampling for one video. `frames`, if given, replaces iter_raw_frames(mp4) as the
    frame source (the threaded pipeline, D-023); `mp4` is then only checked for emptiness."""
    global _CUR_VIDEO
    _CUR_VIDEO = video
    acc = SecondAccumulator(video, w)
    sv = StagedVideo(acc, det, stages, flags)
    n_frames = 0
    try:
        if not mp4:
            raise VideoError("empty or missing mp4 bytes")
        decode_err = None
        gen = iter_raw_frames(mp4) if frames is None else frames
        while True:
            try:
                t, vf, k = next(gen)
            except StopIteration:
                break
            except VideoError as e:
                decode_err = e  # frames decoded before the failure are still used
                break
            s = math.floor(t)
            if s < 0 or (sv.cur is not None and s < sv.cur.s):
                decode_err = VideoError(f"frame timestamp goes back to second {s}")
                break
            sv.add_frame(s, vf, k)
            del vf
            n_frames += 1
        gen.close()
        sv.finish()
        if decode_err is not None:
            raise decode_err
        acc.finish(keep_partial=True)
    except VideoError as e:
        acc.finish(keep_partial=keep_partial)
        w.error(video, str(e))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - never let one video stop the run
        acc.finish(keep_partial=keep_partial)
        w.error(video, f"unexpected {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    w.flush()
    return n_frames


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- threaded pipeline (D-023)

QUEUE_BYTES = 512 << 20    # decoded frames waiting in the queue (YUV bytes)
QUEUE_CHUNK_FRAMES = 32    # frames per queue item
STATS["peak_queue_bytes"] = 0


class _Stopped(Exception):
    """The consumer has stopped; the decoder thread exits."""


class _ByteQueue:
    """FIFO limited by the bytes of the frames it holds. One item is always allowed in,
    so a single large chunk can't block forever."""

    def __init__(self, max_bytes: int):
        import collections
        import threading
        self.max_bytes, self.bytes = max_bytes, 0
        self.items = collections.deque()
        self.cv = threading.Condition()
        self.stopped = False

    def put(self, item, nbytes: int = 0):
        with self.cv:
            while self.items and self.bytes + nbytes > self.max_bytes and not self.stopped:
                self.cv.wait()
            if self.stopped:
                raise _Stopped
            self.items.append((item, nbytes))
            self.bytes += nbytes
            STATS["peak_queue_bytes"] = max(STATS["peak_queue_bytes"], self.bytes)
            self.cv.notify_all()

    def get(self):
        with self.cv:
            while not self.items:
                self.cv.wait()
            item, nbytes = self.items.popleft()
            self.bytes -= nbytes
            self.cv.notify_all()
            return item

    def stop(self):
        with self.cv:
            self.stopped = True
            self.items.clear()
            self.bytes = 0
            self.cv.notify_all()


class FrameProducer:
    """The decoder thread: reads Parquet rows in order and decodes each video with
    iter_raw_frames, sending events to the queue in the same order as run_serial works:
      ("file_problem", name, exc)            footer unreadable
      ("rows_unreadable", name, row, n, exc) rows from `row` on can't be read
      ("video", vid, has_bytes)              then, for a video with bytes, ("frames", list)
                                             chunks and exactly one of ("vend",),
                                             ("verr", VideoError) or ("vexc", exception)
      ("done",) at the end, or ("fatal", exc) first if the thread itself failed.
    """

    def __init__(self, files, only):
        import threading
        self.files, self.only = files, only
        self.q = _ByteQueue(QUEUE_BYTES)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="decoder", daemon=True)

    def start(self):
        self.thread.start()

    def stop(self):
        self.q.stop()
        self.thread.join(timeout=10)

    def _run(self):
        try:
            self._produce()
        except _Stopped:
            return
        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            try:
                self.q.put(("fatal", e))
            except _Stopped:
                return
        try:
            self.q.put(("done",))
        except _Stopped:
            pass

    def _produce(self):
        import pyarrow.parquet as pq

        for path in self.files:
            try:
                pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
                n_rows = pf.metadata.num_rows
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                self.q.put(("file_problem", path.name, e))
                continue
            row = 0
            try:
                for batch in pf.iter_batches(batch_size=1, columns=["mp4"]):
                    for mp4 in batch.column("mp4").to_pylist():
                        vid = f"{path.name}:{row}"
                        if self.only is None or vid in self.only:
                            self._decode(vid, mp4)
                        row += 1
            except _Stopped:
                raise
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - reading failed: like run_serial
                self.q.put(("rows_unreadable", path.name, row, n_rows, e))

    def _decode(self, vid, mp4):
        self.q.put(("video", vid, bool(mp4)))
        if not mp4:
            return
        chunk, nbytes = [], 0
        try:
            for item in iter_raw_frames(mp4):
                chunk.append(item)
                nbytes += frame_bytes(item[1])
                del item
                if len(chunk) >= QUEUE_CHUNK_FRAMES:
                    self.q.put(("frames", chunk), nbytes)
                    chunk, nbytes = [], 0
        except VideoError as e:
            end = ("verr", e)
        except _Stopped:
            raise
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            end = ("vexc", e)
        else:
            end = ("vend",)
        if chunk:
            self.q.put(("frames", chunk), nbytes)
        self.q.put(end)


class _QueuedFrames:
    """Iterator over one video's frames from the queue; raises the decoder's error after the
    frames decoded before it, like iter_raw_frames. Frames are handed over one at a time and
    not kept, so their release is decided only by process_video_staged (D-019)."""

    def __init__(self, q: _ByteQueue):
        import collections
        self.q, self.ended = q, False
        self.terminal = None  # ("done",) or ("fatal", exc) if the stream ended inside this video
        self.items = collections.deque()

    def __iter__(self):
        return self

    def _next_event(self):
        ev = self.q.get()
        if ev[0] in ("fatal", "done"):  # can only happen if the decoder thread failed
            self.ended, self.terminal = True, ev
            raise RuntimeError("decoder thread failed") from (ev[1] if ev[0] == "fatal" else None)
        return ev

    def __next__(self):
        while not self.items:
            if self.ended:
                raise StopIteration
            ev = self._next_event()
            if ev[0] == "frames":
                self.items.extend(ev[1])
                ev[1].clear()
            elif ev[0] == "vend":
                self.ended = True
            else:  # "verr" or "vexc"
                self.ended = True
                raise ev[1]
            del ev
        return self.items.popleft()

    def close(self):
        """Skip whatever is left of this video (after an early stop, e.g. a timestamp going back)."""
        self.items.clear()
        while not self.ended:
            try:
                ev = self._next_event()
            except RuntimeError:
                return
            if ev[0] in ("vend", "verr", "vexc"):
                self.ended = True
            elif ev[0] == "frames":
                ev[1].clear()


def _log_video(vid, nf, inferred, t_v):
    print(f"{vid} frames={nf} inferred={inferred} {time.time() - t_v:.1f}s", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def _file_problem(msg, file_problems):
    print(f"WARNING {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    file_problems.append(msg)


def run_serial(files, only, det, w, keep_partial, sampling) -> tuple[int, int, list]:
    """The single-threaded loop (D-015, D-017): read, decode and infer in turn. The fallback."""
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    n_videos = n_frames = 0
    file_problems = []
    for path in files:
        try:
            pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
            n_rows = pf.metadata.num_rows
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - footer unreadable: no valid video IDs (D-015 #2)
            _file_problem(f"{path.name}: unreadable Parquet file ({type(e).__name__}: {e})", file_problems)
            continue
        row = 0
        try:
            for batch in pf.iter_batches(batch_size=1, columns=["mp4"]):
                for mp4 in batch.column("mp4").to_pylist():
                    vid = f"{path.name}:{row}"
                    if only is not None and vid not in only:
                        row += 1
                        continue
                    t_v, inf0 = time.time(), det.n_frames
                    if SAMPLING[sampling] is None:
                        nf = process_video(vid, mp4, det, w, keep_partial)
                    else:
                        stages, flags = SAMPLING[sampling]
                        nf = process_video_staged(vid, mp4, det, w, keep_partial, stages, flags)
                    n_videos += 1
                    n_frames += nf
                    _log_video(vid, nf, det.n_frames - inf0, t_v)
                    row += 1
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - data unreadable: an error line for each remaining row
            for r in range(row, n_rows):
                w.error(f"{path.name}:{r}", f"could not read row: {type(e).__name__}")
            w.flush()
            _file_problem(f"{path.name}: rows {row}..{n_rows - 1} unreadable ({type(e).__name__}: {e})",
                          file_problems)
    return n_videos, n_frames, file_problems


def run_threaded(files, only, det, w, keep_partial, sampling) -> tuple[int, int, list]:
    """Decoding in a separate thread, overlapped with inference (D-023). The main thread does
    exactly what run_serial does, in the same order, on the same frames."""
    stages, flags = SAMPLING[sampling]
    prod = FrameProducer(files, only)
    prod.start()
    n_videos = n_frames = 0
    file_problems = []
    try:
        while True:
            ev = prod.q.get()
            kind = ev[0]
            if kind == "done":
                break
            if kind == "fatal":
                raise RuntimeError("decoder thread failed") from ev[1]
            if kind == "file_problem":
                _, name, e = ev
                _file_problem(f"{name}: unreadable Parquet file ({type(e).__name__}: {e})", file_problems)
            elif kind == "rows_unreadable":
                _, name, row, n_rows, e = ev
                for r in range(row, n_rows):
                    w.error(f"{name}:{r}", f"could not read row: {type(e).__name__}")
                w.flush()
                _file_problem(f"{name}: rows {row}..{n_rows - 1} unreadable ({type(e).__name__}: {e})",
                              file_problems)
            elif kind == "video":
                _, vid, has_bytes = ev
                t_v, inf0 = time.time(), det.n_frames
                frames = _QueuedFrames(prod.q) if has_bytes else None
                nf = process_video_staged(vid, has_bytes, det, w, keep_partial, stages, flags,
                                          frames=frames)
                if frames is not None:
                    frames.close()
                    if frames.terminal is not None:  # the decoder thread failed inside this video
                        if frames.terminal[0] == "fatal":
                            raise RuntimeError("decoder thread failed") from frames.terminal[1]
                        break
                n_videos += 1
                n_frames += nf
                _log_video(vid, nf, det.n_frames - inf0, t_v)
            del ev
    finally:
        prod.stop()
    return n_videos, n_frames, file_problems


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="folder of .parquet files")
    ap.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="output .jsonl path")
    ap.add_argument("--weights", default=str(HERE / "weights" / "yolo11l.pt"))
    ap.add_argument("--drop-partial-second", action="store_true",
                    help="after a failure partway through, drop the unfinished second (D-015 #3)")
    ap.add_argument("--sampling", choices=list(SAMPLING), default=DEFAULT_SAMPLING,
                    help="which frames go through the model (D-017); 'all' is the every-frame fallback")
    ap.add_argument("--precision", choices=["fp32", "fp16"], default="fp16",
                    help="model precision; fp16 was promoted in D-022, fp32 is the fallback")
    ap.add_argument("--pipeline", choices=["serial", "threaded"], default="threaded",
                    help="threaded (default, D-023): decode in a separate thread, overlapped with "
                         "inference; serial: the single-threaded fallback")
    ap.add_argument("--engine", default="auto",
                    help="TensorRT engine (D-025): 'auto' (default: weights/yolo11l.engine from prep.py if "
                         "present, else PyTorch FP16), 'off', or a path")
    ap.add_argument("--only-videos", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # dev only: subset manifest JSON
    ap.add_argument("--log-inferred", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # dev only: frames sent to the model
    a = ap.parse_args()
    global INFER_LOG
    if a.log_inferred:
        INFER_LOG = open(a.log_inferred, "w", buffering=1 << 20)

    only = None
    if a.only_videos:  # validation use only: keep row numbers as they are and skip other rows
        only = {v["video"] for v in json.loads(Path(a.only_videos).read_text())["videos"]}

    t_start = time.time()
    files = sorted(Path(a.input).glob("*.parquet"))  # D-015 #1
    engine = None
    if a.engine == "auto":
        cand = Path(a.weights).with_suffix(".engine")
        engine = cand if cand.exists() else None
        if engine is None:
            print(f"WARNING no TensorRT engine at {cand} (run prep.py); using PyTorch", file=sys.stderr)
    elif a.engine != "off":
        engine = Path(a.engine)
    det = Detector(Path(a.weights), half=a.precision == "fp16", engine=engine)
    w = Writer(a.output)
    keep_partial = not a.drop_partial_second
    pipeline = a.pipeline if SAMPLING[a.sampling] is not None else "serial"  # 'all' is serial only
    runner = run_threaded if pipeline == "threaded" else run_serial
    n_videos, n_frames, file_problems = runner(files, only, det, w, keep_partial, a.sampling)

    w.close()
    if INFER_LOG is not None:
        INFER_LOG.close()
    dt = time.time() - t_start
    print(f"DONE sampling={a.sampling} precision={a.precision} backend={det.backend} pipeline={pipeline} "
          f"peak_queue_mb={STATS['peak_queue_bytes'] / 2**20:.0f} files={len(files)} videos={n_videos} frames={n_frames} "
          f"inferred={det.n_frames} predict_calls={det.n_calls} oom_retries={det.n_oom} "
          f"peak_buffered_frames={STATS['peak_buffered_frames']} "
          f"peak_buffered_mb={STATS['peak_buffered_bytes'] / 2**20:.0f} "
          f"overflow_seconds={STATS['overflow_seconds']} "
          f"seconds={w.n_seconds} errors={w.n_errors} file_problems={len(file_problems)} "
          f"wall={dt:.1f}s fps={n_frames / max(dt, 1e-9):.1f}", file=sys.stderr)
    for m in file_problems:
        print(f"INCOMPLETE {m}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0  # data problems never make the exit code nonzero (D-015 #2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

6	(person, car, dog, laptop, cell phone) are present and how many people are visible,

66	class SecondAccumulator:
67	    """Groups per-frame results into seconds (brief §5) and writes each second once it's complete.
68	
69	    A second is complete when a frame from a later second arrives. Seconds with no frames
70	    in between are written as empty. A frame that belongs to a second that has already
71	    been written is an error (D-015 C1).
72	    """
73	
74	    def __init__(self, video: str, writer: Writer):
75	        self.video, self.w = video, writer
76	        self.cur = None          # second currently being collected
77	        self.next_to_write = 0   # every second below this has been written
78	        self._reset()

113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- decoding
114	
115	def rotation_k(frame, stream) -> int:
116	    """How many 90° counterclockwise turns np.rot90 needs (D-015 C3).
117	
118	    frame.rotation is in degrees counterclockwise, from the display matrix. If it's
119	    missing, the old `rotate` stream tag is used, which is in degrees clockwise.
120	    """
121	    ccw = getattr(frame, "rotation", None)
122	    if not ccw:
123	        tag = (stream.metadata or {}).get("rotate")
124	        ccw = -int(float(tag)) if tag not in (None, "") else 0
125	    return int(round(ccw / 90.0)) % 4
126	
127	
128	def frame_to_bgr(vf, k: int):
129	    """Convert one decoded frame to a BGR array and apply its rotation (D-015 C3)."""
130	    import numpy as np
131	
132	    img = vf.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
133	    if k:
134	        img = np.ascontiguousarray(np.rot90(img, k=k))
135	    return img
136	
137	
138	def frame_bytes(vf) -> int:
139	    """About how much memory a buffered YUV 4:2:0 frame holds (0 for a released frame)."""
140	    if vf is None:
141	        return 0
142	    try:
143	        return vf.width * vf.height * 3 // 2
144	    except AttributeError:
145	        return 1

148	def iter_raw_frames(mp4: bytes):
149	    """Yield (t_rel: Fraction, decoded frame, rotation k) for every frame, in presentation order.
150	
151	    t_rel is the time since the first decoded frame (D-015 C4). The frame isn't converted
152	    yet, so frames that are never sent to the model cost only the decode. Raises
153	    VideoError on any decoding problem. Frames already yielded stay valid.
154	    """
155	    import av
156	
157	    try:
158	        container = av.open(io.BytesIO(mp4), mode="r")
159	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
160	        raise VideoError(f"could not open video: {type(e).__name__}") from e
161	    with container:
162	        if not container.streams.video:
163	            raise VideoError("no video stream")
164	        stream = container.streams.video[0]
165	        t0 = None
166	        try:
167	            for frame in container.decode(stream):
168	                if frame.pts is None:
169	                    raise VideoError("frame without timestamp")
170	                tb = frame.time_base or stream.time_base
171	                t = frame.pts * Fraction(tb.numerator, tb.denominator)
172	                if t0 is None:
173	                    t0 = t
174	                yield t - t0, frame, rotation_k(frame, stream)
175	        except VideoError:
176	            raise
177	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
178	            raise VideoError(f"decode failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}") from e
179	        if t0 is None:
180	            raise VideoError("no decodable frames")
181	
182	
183	def iter_frames(mp4: bytes):
184	    """Yield (t_rel: Fraction, bgr ndarray) for every decoded frame (the every-frame path)."""
185	    for t, vf, k in iter_raw_frames(mp4):
186	        yield t, frame_to_bgr(vf, k)

192	    def __init__(self, weights: Path, half: bool = False, engine: Path | None = None):

229	    def _predict(self, imgs):
230	        """One predict call on same-shape images (D-015 C2)."""
231	        try:
232	            # FP32 calls stay exactly as before; an engine has its precision built in
233	            extra = {"quantize": 16} if self.half and self.backend == "pytorch" else {}
234	            out = self.model.predict(imgs, device=self.device, **extra, **PREDICT_KW)
235	        finally:
236	            self._release_predictor_state()
237	        self.n_calls += 1
238	        self.n_frames += len(imgs)
239	        return out
240	
241	    def _summarise(self, r) -> tuple[list[bool], int]:
242	        present = [False] * len(TARGETS)
243	        n_people = 0
244	        for c in r.boxes.cls.tolist():
245	            k = self.target_of.get(int(c))
246	            if k is not None:
247	                present[k] = True
248	                n_people += k == PERSON
249	        return present, n_people
250	
251	    @staticmethod
252	    def _is_oom(e: BaseException) -> bool:
253	        import torch
254	        return isinstance(e, torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError) or (
255	            isinstance(e, RuntimeError) and "out of memory" in str(e).lower())
256	
257	    def detect(self, imgs) -> list[tuple[list[bool], int]]:
258	        """For each image: (which targets are present, person count).
259	
260	        Images are sent in runs of the same shape, never more than the batch size known to
261	        fit for that shape. On CUDA out-of-memory (D-015 C5, D-019):
262	          - the retry happens only after leaving the `except` block, so the exception's
263	            traceback, which references the failed attempt's GPU tensors, is already gone;
264	          - the predictor's leftover state is dropped, garbage is collected and the CUDA
265	            cache is emptied;
266	          - the batch size for that shape is halved, and stays halved for later batches;
267	          - an OOM on a single frame is a VideoError for this video only.
268	        """
269	        out, i = [], 0
270	        while i < len(imgs):
271	            shape = imgs[i].shape
272	            j = i + 1
273	            while j < len(imgs) and imgs[j].shape == shape:
274	                j += 1
275	            n = min(j - i, self.batch_cap.get(shape, j - i))
276	            failed = False
277	            try:
278	                results = self._predict(imgs[i:i + n])
279	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
280	                if not self._is_oom(e):
281	                    raise
282	                failed = True
283	            if failed:  # outside the except block: the traceback has been released
284	                self.n_oom += 1
285	                self._recover_from_oom()
286	                if n == 1:
287	                    raise VideoError("CUDA out of memory on a single frame")
288	                self.batch_cap[shape] = n // 2
289	                continue
290	            out += [self._summarise(r) for r in results]
291	            del results
292	            i += n
293	        return out
294	
295	    def _recover_from_oom(self):
296	        import gc
297	
298	        self._release_predictor_state()
299	        gc.collect()
300	        if self.torch.cuda.is_available():
301	            self.torch.cuda.empty_cache()

306	def process_video(video: str, mp4, det: Detector, w: Writer, keep_partial: bool) -> int:
307	    acc = SecondAccumulator(video, w)
308	    batch_t, batch_img, batch_bytes, n_frames = [], [], 0, 0
309	
310	    def flush_batch():
311	        nonlocal batch_bytes
312	        if batch_img:
313	            for t, (present, n_people) in zip(batch_t, det.detect(batch_img)):
314	                acc.add(math.floor(t), present, n_people)
315	        batch_t.clear()
316	        batch_img.clear()
317	        batch_bytes = 0
318	
319	    try:
320	        if not mp4:
321	            raise VideoError("empty or missing mp4 bytes")
322	        try:
323	            for t, img in iter_frames(mp4):  # batches never mix videos (D-015 C2)
324	                batch_t.append(t)
325	                batch_img.append(img)
326	                batch_bytes += img.nbytes
327	                n_frames += 1
328	                if len(batch_img) >= MAX_BATCH_FRAMES or batch_bytes >= MAX_BATCH_BYTES:
329	                    flush_batch()
330	        except VideoError:
331	            flush_batch()  # frames decoded before the failure are still valid
332	            raise
333	        flush_batch()
334	        acc.finish(keep_partial=True)
335	    except VideoError as e:
336	        acc.finish(keep_partial=keep_partial)
337	        w.error(video, str(e))
338	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - never let one video stop the run
339	        acc.finish(keep_partial=keep_partial)
340	        w.error(video, f"unexpected {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
341	    w.flush()
342	    return n_frames

567	def process_video_staged(video: str, mp4, det, w: Writer, keep_partial: bool, stages, flags,
568	                         frames=None) -> int:
569	    """Staged sampling for one video. `frames`, if given, replaces iter_raw_frames(mp4) as the
570	    frame source (the threaded pipeline, D-023); `mp4` is then only checked for emptiness."""
571	    global _CUR_VIDEO
572	    _CUR_VIDEO = video
573	    acc = SecondAccumulator(video, w)
574	    sv = StagedVideo(acc, det, stages, flags)
575	    n_frames = 0
576	    try:
577	        if not mp4:
578	            raise VideoError("empty or missing mp4 bytes")
579	        decode_err = None
580	        gen = iter_raw_frames(mp4) if frames is None else frames
581	        while True:
582	            try:
583	                t, vf, k = next(gen)
584	            except StopIteration:
585	                break
586	            except VideoError as e:
587	                decode_err = e  # frames decoded before the failure are still used
588	                break
589	            s = math.floor(t)
590	            if s < 0 or (sv.cur is not None and s < sv.cur.s):
591	                decode_err = VideoError(f"frame timestamp goes back to second {s}")
592	                break
593	            sv.add_frame(s, vf, k)
594	            del vf
595	            n_frames += 1
596	        gen.close()
597	        sv.finish()
598	        if decode_err is not None:
599	            raise decode_err
600	        acc.finish(keep_partial=True)
601	    except VideoError as e:
602	        acc.finish(keep_partial=keep_partial)
603	        w.error(video, str(e))
604	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - never let one video stop the run
605	        acc.finish(keep_partial=keep_partial)
606	        w.error(video, f"unexpected {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
607	    w.flush()
608	    return n_frames

611	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- threaded pipeline (D-023)
612	
613	QUEUE_BYTES = 512 << 20    # decoded frames waiting in the queue (YUV bytes)
614	QUEUE_CHUNK_FRAMES = 32    # frames per queue item
615	STATS["peak_queue_bytes"] = 0
616	
617	
618	class _Stopped(Exception):
619	    """The consumer has stopped; the decoder thread exits."""
620	
621	
622	class _ByteQueue:
623	    """FIFO limited by the bytes of the frames it holds. One item is always allowed in,
624	    so a single large chunk can't block forever."""
625	
626	    def __init__(self, max_bytes: int):
627	        import collections
628	        import threading
629	        self.max_bytes, self.bytes = max_bytes, 0
630	        self.items = collections.deque()
631	        self.cv = threading.Condition()
632	        self.stopped = False
633	
634	    def put(self, item, nbytes: int = 0):
635	        with self.cv:
636	            while self.items and self.bytes + nbytes > self.max_bytes and not self.stopped:
637	                self.cv.wait()
638	            if self.stopped:
639	                raise _Stopped
640	            self.items.append((item, nbytes))
641	            self.bytes += nbytes
642	            STATS["peak_queue_bytes"] = max(STATS["peak_queue_bytes"], self.bytes)
643	            self.cv.notify_all()
644	
645	    def get(self):
646	        with self.cv:
647	            while not self.items:
648	                self.cv.wait()
649	            item, nbytes = self.items.popleft()
650	            self.bytes -= nbytes
651	            self.cv.notify_all()
652	            return item
653	
654	    def stop(self):
655	        with self.cv:
656	            self.stopped = True
657	            self.items.clear()
658	            self.bytes = 0
659	            self.cv.notify_all()
660

662	class FrameProducer:
663	    """The decoder thread: reads Parquet rows in order and decodes each video with
664	    iter_raw_frames, sending events to the queue in the same order as run_serial works:
665	      ("file_problem", name, exc)            footer unreadable
666	      ("rows_unreadable", name, row, n, exc) rows from `row` on can't be read
667	      ("video", vid, has_bytes)              then, for a video with bytes, ("frames", list)
668	                                             chunks and exactly one of ("vend",),
669	                                             ("verr", VideoError) or ("vexc", exception)
670	      ("done",) at the end, or ("fatal", exc) first if the thread itself failed.
671	    """
672	
673	    def __init__(self, files, only):
674	        import threading
675	        self.files, self.only = files, only
676	        self.q = _ByteQueue(QUEUE_BYTES)
677	        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="decoder", daemon=True)
678	
679	    def start(self):
680	        self.thread.start()
681	
682	    def stop(self):
683	        self.q.stop()
684	        self.thread.join(timeout=10)
685	
686	    def _run(self):
687	        try:
688	            self._produce()
689	        except _Stopped:
690	            return
691	        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001
692	            try:
693	                self.q.put(("fatal", e))
694	            except _Stopped:
695	                return
696	        try:
697	            self.q.put(("done",))
698	        except _Stopped:
699	            pass
700	
701	    def _produce(self):
702	        import pyarrow.parquet as pq
703	
704	        for path in self.files:
705	            try:
706	                pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
707	                n_rows = pf.metadata.num_rows
708	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
709	                self.q.put(("file_problem", path.name, e))
710	                continue
711	            row = 0
712	            try:
713	                for batch in pf.iter_batches(batch_size=1, columns=["mp4"]):
714	                    for mp4 in batch.column("mp4").to_pylist():
715	                        vid = f"{path.name}:{row}"
716	                        if self.only is None or vid in self.only:
717	                            self._decode(vid, mp4)
718	                        row += 1
719	            except _Stopped:
720	                raise
721	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - reading failed: like run_serial
722	                self.q.put(("rows_unreadable", path.name, row, n_rows, e))
723	
724	    def _decode(self, vid, mp4):
725	        self.q.put(("video", vid, bool(mp4)))
726	        if not mp4:
727	            return
728	        chunk, nbytes = [], 0
729	        try:
730	            for item in iter_raw_frames(mp4):
731	                chunk.append(item)
732	                nbytes += frame_bytes(item[1])
733	                del item
734	                if len(chunk) >= QUEUE_CHUNK_FRAMES:
735	                    self.q.put(("frames", chunk), nbytes)
736	                    chunk, nbytes = [], 0
737	        except VideoError as e:
738	            end = ("verr", e)
739	        except _Stopped:
740	            raise
741	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
742	            end = ("vexc", e)
743	        else:
744	            end = ("vend",)
745	        if chunk:
746	            self.q.put(("frames", chunk), nbytes)
747	        self.q.put(end)
748

750	class _QueuedFrames:
751	    """Iterator over one video's frames from the queue; raises the decoder's error after the
752	    frames decoded before it, like iter_raw_frames. Frames are handed over one at a time and
753	    not kept, so their release is decided only by process_video_staged (D-019)."""
754	
755	    def __init__(self, q: _ByteQueue):
756	        import collections
757	        self.q, self.ended = q, False
758	        self.terminal = None  # ("done",) or ("fatal", exc) if the stream ended inside this video
759	        self.items = collections.deque()
760	
761	    def __iter__(self):
762	        return self
763	
764	    def _next_event(self):
765	        ev = self.q.get()
766	        if ev[0] in ("fatal", "done"):  # can only happen if the decoder thread failed
767	            self.ended, self.terminal = True, ev
768	            raise RuntimeError("decoder thread failed") from (ev[1] if ev[0] == "fatal" else None)
769	        return ev
770	
771	    def __next__(self):
772	        while not self.items:
773	            if self.ended:
774	                raise StopIteration
775	            ev = self._next_event()
776	            if ev[0] == "frames":
777	                self.items.extend(ev[1])
778	                ev[1].clear()
779	            elif ev[0] == "vend":
780	                self.ended = True
781	            else:  # "verr" or "vexc"
782	                self.ended = True
783	                raise ev[1]
784	            del ev
785	        return self.items.popleft()
786	
787	    def close(self):
788	        """Skip whatever is left of this video (after an early stop, e.g. a timestamp going back)."""
789	        self.items.clear()
790	        while not self.ended:
791	            try:
792	                ev = self._next_event()
793	            except RuntimeError:
794	                return
795	            if ev[0] in ("vend", "verr", "vexc"):
796	                self.ended = True
797	            elif ev[0] == "frames":
798	                ev[1].clear()
799

810	def run_serial(files, only, det, w, keep_partial, sampling) -> tuple[int, int, list]:
811	    """The single-threaded loop (D-015, D-017): read, decode and infer in turn. The fallback."""
812	    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
813	
814	    n_videos = n_frames = 0
815	    file_problems = []
816	    for path in files:
817	        try:
818	            pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
819	            n_rows = pf.metadata.num_rows
820	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - footer unreadable: no valid video IDs (D-015 #2)
821	            _file_problem(f"{path.name}: unreadable Parquet file ({type(e).__name__}: {e})", file_problems)
822	            continue
823	        row = 0
824	        try:
825	            for batch in pf.iter_batches(batch_size=1, columns=["mp4"]):
826	                for mp4 in batch.column("mp4").to_pylist():
827	                    vid = f"{path.name}:{row}"
828	                    if only is not None and vid not in only:
829	                        row += 1
830	                        continue
831	                    t_v, inf0 = time.time(), det.n_frames
832	                    if SAMPLING[sampling] is None:
833	                        nf = process_video(vid, mp4, det, w, keep_partial)
834	                    else:
835	                        stages, flags = SAMPLING[sampling]
836	                        nf = process_video_staged(vid, mp4, det, w, keep_partial, stages, flags)
837	                    n_videos += 1
838	                    n_frames += nf
839	                    _log_video(vid, nf, det.n_frames - inf0, t_v)
840	                    row += 1
841	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - data unreadable: an error line for each remaining row
842	            for r in range(row, n_rows):
843	                w.error(f"{path.name}:{r}", f"could not read row: {type(e).__name__}")
844	            w.flush()
845	            _file_problem(f"{path.name}: rows {row}..{n_rows - 1} unreadable ({type(e).__name__}: {e})",
846	                          file_problems)
847	    return n_videos, n_frames, file_problems

850	def run_threaded(files, only, det, w, keep_partial, sampling) -> tuple[int, int, list]:
851	    """Decoding in a separate thread, overlapped with inference (D-023). The main thread does
852	    exactly what run_serial does, in the same order, on the same frames."""

854	    prod = FrameProducer(files, only)
855	    prod.start()
856	    n_videos = n_frames = 0
857	    file_problems = []
858	    try:
859	        while True:
860	            ev = prod.q.get()
861	            kind = ev[0]
862	            if kind == "done":
863	                break
864	            if kind == "fatal":
865	                raise RuntimeError("decoder thread failed") from ev[1]
866	            if kind == "file_problem":
867	                _, name, e = ev
868	                _file_problem(f"{name}: unreadable Parquet file ({type(e).__name__}: {e})", file_problems)
869	            elif kind == "rows_unreadable":
870	                _, name, row, n_rows, e = ev
871	                for r in range(row, n_rows):
872	                    w.error(f"{name}:{r}", f"could not read row: {type(e).__name__}")
873	                w.flush()
874	                _file_problem(f"{name}: rows {row}..{n_rows - 1} unreadable ({type(e).__name__}: {e})",
875	                              file_problems)
876	            elif kind == "video":
877	                _, vid, has_bytes = ev
878	                t_v, inf0 = time.time(), det.n_frames
879	                frames = _QueuedFrames(prod.q) if has_bytes else None
880	                nf = process_video_staged(vid, has_bytes, det, w, keep_partial, stages, flags,
881	                                          frames=frames)
882	                if frames is not None:
883	                    frames.close()
884	                    if frames.terminal is not None:  # the decoder thread failed inside this video
885	                        if frames.terminal[0] == "fatal":
886	                            raise RuntimeError("decoder thread failed") from frames.terminal[1]
887	                        break
888	                n_videos += 1
889	                n_frames += nf
890	                _log_video(vid, nf, det.n_frames - inf0, t_v)
891	            del ev
892	    finally:

912	                         "inference; serial: the single-threaded fallback")

915	                         "present, else PyTorch FP16), 'off', or a path")
916	    ap.add_argument("--only-videos", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # dev only: subset manifest JSON
917	    ap.add_argument("--log-inferred", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # dev only: frames sent to the model
918	    a = ap.parse_args()

924	    if a.only_videos:  # validation use only: keep row numbers as they are and skip other rows
925	        only = {v["video"] for v in json.loads(Path(a.only_videos).read_text())["videos"]}

def load(path):
    secs, errs, dups, bad = {}, {}, [], []
    for n, line in enumerate(open(path), 1):
        r = json.loads(line)
        if "error" in r:
            errs[r["video"]] = r["error"]
            continue
        key = (r["video"], r["second"])
        if key in secs:
            dups.append(key)
        if (not isinstance(r.get("objects"), list) or any(o not in TARGETS for o in r["objects"])
                or not isinstance(r.get("people"), int)):
            bad.append(n)
        secs[key] = (frozenset(r["objects"]), r["people"])
    return secs, errs, dups, bad


def f1(tp, fp, fn):
    d = 2 * tp + fp + fn
    return 1.0 if d == 0 else 2 * tp / d


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--ref", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pred", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--json-out")
    ap.add_argument("--worst", type=int, default=10)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    ref, ref_err, _, _ = load(a.ref)
    pred, pred_err, dups, bad = load(a.pred)
    extra = [k for k in pred if k not in ref]
    missing = [k for k in ref if k not in pred]

    tp, fp, fn = Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
    exact = within1 = 0
    sample_f1 = 0.0
    per_video = defaultdict(lambda: Counter())
    for key, (robj, rpeople) in ref.items():
        pobj, ppeople = pred.get(key, (frozenset(), None))
        for c in TARGETS:
            tp[c] += (c in robj) and (c in pobj)
            fp[c] += (c not in robj) and (c in pobj)
            fn[c] += (c in robj) and (c not in pobj)
        s_tp = len(robj & pobj)
        sample_f1 += f1(s_tp, len(pobj - robj), len(robj - pobj))
        ok_exact = ppeople == rpeople
        ok_w1 = ppeople is not None and abs(ppeople - rpeople) <= 1
        exact += ok_exact
        within1 += ok_w1
        v = per_video[key[0]]
        v["seconds"] += 1
        v["people_exact"] += ok_exact
        v["obj_err"] += len(robj ^ pobj)

    n = len(ref)
    per_class = {c: f1(tp[c], fp[c], fn[c]) for c in TARGETS}
    micro = f1(sum(tp.values()), sum(fp.values()), sum(fn.values()))
    macro_classes = [c for c in TARGETS if tp[c] + fp[c] + fn[c] > 0]
    macro = sum(per_class[c] for c in macro_classes) / max(len(macro_classes), 1)
    res = {
        "seconds_ref": n,
        "seconds_pred": len(pred),
        "missing_seconds": len(missing),
        "extra_seconds": len(extra),
        "duplicate_lines": len(dups),
        "malformed_lines": len(bad),
        "error_videos_pred": len(pred_err),
        "error_videos_ref": len(ref_err),
        "f1_micro": micro,
        "f1_macro": macro,
        "f1_gate": min(micro, macro),
        "f1_sample_avg_info_only": sample_f1 / max(n, 1),
        "f1_per_class": per_class,
        "class_counts": {c: {"tp": tp[c], "fp": fp[c], "fn": fn[c]} for c in TARGETS},
        "people_exact": exact / max(n, 1),
        "people_within1": within1 / max(n, 1),
    }
    complete = not (extra or dups or bad)
    res["complete"] = complete
    res["pass"] = (complete and res["f1_gate"] >= THRESH["f1"]
                   and res["people_exact"] >= THRESH["people_exact"]
                   and res["people_within1"] >= THRESH["people_within1"])

    print(f"seconds ref={n} pred={len(pred)} missing={len(missing)} extra={len(extra)} "
          f"dups={len(dups)} malformed={len(bad)} errors(pred)={len(pred_err)}")
    print(f"F1 micro={micro:.4f} macro={macro:.4f} gate={res['f1_gate']:.4f} "
          f"(sample-avg {res['f1_sample_avg_info_only']:.4f}, info only)")
    print("F1 per class: " + "  ".join(f"{c}={per_class[c]:.4f}" for c in TARGETS))
    print(f"people exact={res['people_exact']:.4f} within1={res['people_within1']:.4f}")
    print(f"PASS={res['pass']}  (gate f1>={THRESH['f1']}, exact>={THRESH['people_exact']}, "
          f"within1>={THRESH['people_within1']}, complete={complete})")
    if a.worst:
        worst = sorted(per_video.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["people_exact"] / kv[1]["seconds"])
        print(f"worst {a.worst} videos by people-exact:")
        for vid, v in worst[: a.worst]:
            print(f"  {vid}: exact {v['people_exact'] / v['seconds']:.3f} "
                  f"obj_err {v['obj_err']} over {v['seconds']} s")
    if a.json_out:
        json.dump(res, open(a.json_out, "w"), indent=1)
    sys.exit(0 if res["pass"] else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def sha256(p: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 22), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def get_weights():
    WEIGHTS.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if not WEIGHTS.exists():
        print(f"downloading {URL}")
        tmp = WEIGHTS.with_suffix(".part")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(URL, timeout=120) as r, open(tmp, "wb") as f:
            shutil.copyfileobj(r, f)
        tmp.rename(WEIGHTS)
    got = sha256(WEIGHTS)
    if got != SHA256:
        raise SystemExit(f"{WEIGHTS} sha256 {got} is not the official yolo11l.pt ({SHA256})")
    print(f"weights ok: {WEIGHTS} ({got[:12]}...)")


def build_engine(force: bool):
    import tensorrt as trt
    import torch
    from ultralytics import YOLO

    meta_path = ENGINE.with_suffix(".engine.json")
    want = {"tensorrt": trt.__version__, "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
            "export": {k: v for k, v in EXPORT_KW.items() if k != "device"}, "weights_sha256": SHA256}
    if ENGINE.exists() and meta_path.exists() and not force:
        have = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        if {k: have.get(k) for k in want} == want:
            print(f"engine up to date: {ENGINE}")
            return
    t0 = time.time()
    out = YOLO(str(WEIGHTS)).export(**EXPORT_KW)
    if Path(out).resolve() != ENGINE.resolve():
        shutil.move(out, ENGINE)
    meta_path.write_text(json.dumps({**want, "built_seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)}, indent=1))
    print(f"built {ENGINE} in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s with TensorRT {trt.__version__} on {want['gpu']}")


def check_engine():
    import numpy as np
    from ultralytics import YOLO

    m = YOLO(str(ENGINE), task="detect")
    imgs = [np.full((360, 640, 3), 114, np.uint8)] * 32
    r = m.predict(imgs, imgsz=640, conf=0.4, iou=0.7, verbose=False, device=0)
    assert len(r) == 32
    print(f"engine loads and runs a batch of 32: ok ({len(m.names)} classes)")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="rebuild the engine even if it is up to date")
    ap.add_argument("--no-engine", action="store_true", help="only fetch the weights")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    get_weights()
    if a.no_engine:
        return
    build_engine(a.force)
    check_engine()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

input.content:
# Documentation audit

Audit of `APPROACH.md`, `README.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HARDWARE.md` and `ai_chats/README.md` against the code, the tests and the raw benchmark artifacts. Audit date: 2026-11-21, at commit `e462731`.

- `WRITEUP.md` was not audited (brief §8), and it doesn't exist yet.
- `validation/` contains no other Markdown files.
- No documentation, code, logs or git history were changed during this pass.

**Evidence used:**
- **Code, read statically:** `run.py`, `prep.py`, `requirements.txt` and the `validation/` tools.
- **Ultralytics 8.4.215 source** in the server's venv.
- **Raw logs** on the development server (`~/alethia/work/*/`): every `DONE` line, `/usr/bin/time -v` output, `profile/p0.json`, `sampling/sim.json` and `cleantest/pip_attempt3.log`.
- **The chat transcript**, for test output that was only printed to the terminal.
- **Checks re-run for this audit, all CPU-only:**
  - `validation/test_run_unit.py`: 23 of 23 pass;
  - `validation/check_full_results.py` on the frozen results for files 00000 and 00001: `COMPLETE=True`;
  - set-disjointness checks on the subset manifests;
  - `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()`;
  - `free -b` and `lscpu`.
- **Not re-run:** no GPU job, dataset run, download or engine build was performed.

**Status key:**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| VERIFIED | Directly supported by executable code and/or reproducible evidence. |
| PARTIALLY VERIFIED | Supported only under stated conditions. |
| INACCURATE | Contradicted by the implementation or evidence. |
| OUTDATED | Was true historically but no longer describes the current version. |
| UNVERIFIABLE | The available evidence is insufficient to establish it. |

---

## A. Executive summary

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Substantive claims checked (register in section H) | **112** |
| VERIFIED | **84** |
| PARTIALLY VERIFIED | **16** |
| INACCURATE | **6** |
| OUTDATED | **4** |
| UNVERIFIABLE | **2** |

**Overall assessment:** the documentation is reliable on what the code does and on the measured numbers.

- **Implementation:** the sampling rule, aggregation, timestamps, model settings, fallback, OOM handling and threading all match the code exactly.
- **Measurements:** every wall time, frame count and accuracy figure checked against a raw log or result file matches, and every speed-up ratio recalculates correctly.

**The problems are of three kinds:**
1. **Deployment claims are stated more strongly than the evidence supports.**
   - APPROACH.md describes the clean-environment test without saying that the final install was done with uv from a cache, not with pip.
   - Offline operation was tested only at the Python socket level.
   - Compatibility with the graders' driver and their RTX 4090 is an expectation, not something tested.
2. **Memory figures use inconsistent units.** `/usr/bin/time` reports KiB, but the docs treat the values as kB and call the result GB.
3. **Some details are left out or stale.** These include chunk size, queue accounting and error-path behaviour, plus stale statuses in DECISIONS.md.

There are **no Critical findings**, **1 High**, **5 Medium**, and the rest are Low.

---

## B. Findings

| ID | Severity | Document and lines | Claim | Actual behaviour and evidence | Status | Proposed correction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | **High** | APPROACH.md 293–296 (section 8, "Clean-environment test") | "Setup: a fresh venv and a fresh copy of the repository, then `prep.py`, then offline runs…", presented as a clean-environment test of the deployment. | D-027 and `cleantest/pip_attempt{1,2,3}.log`: **pip never finished an install.** Attempt 1 timed out. Attempt 2 failed resolution and led to the URL pins. Attempt 3 resolved all 67 pinned packages, but was stopped during the final downloads because the route from this server to PyPI ran at about 39 kB/s. The venv that was tested came from `uv pip install` using uv's cache, plus two wheels from a PyPI mirror whose sha256 matches PyPI's. The copy of the repo was `git archive HEAD`, not a clone. | PARTIALLY VERIFIED | See G-1. |

The RTX 4090 is `sm_89`, so the PyTorch fallback relies on the `sm_86` code running there. That is expected, but untested. | PARTIALLY VERIFIED | See G-2. |

**G-1 (F-01)** APPROACH.md lines 293–296. Replace the "Clean-environment test" bullet with:

> - **Clean-environment test (D-027):** a fresh Python 3.11 venv and a fresh copy of the committed repository on the same server. `pip install -r requirements.txt` resolved every pinned package, but this server's route to PyPI was too slow (about 39 kB/s) for pip to finish downloading. Then `pip check`, `prep.py` and offline runs on dev and the holdout: dev F1 0.9918, people exact 0.9920, within ±1 0.9998; holdout 0.9935 / 0.9933 / 0.9999. All 17 fixtures and 23 unit tests passed. A complete `pip install` on a fresh Ubuntu 22.04 machine has not been observed.

**G-2 (F-02)** README.md line 7:

> No `apt-get` packages are needed: PyAV ships its own FFmpeg, and OpenCV is the headless build. Tested with Python 3.11.16 on Ubuntu 26.04 with NVIDIA driver 595.99 (a Quadro RTX 6000). The pinned packages are CUDA 12.6 builds, which need a driver with CUDA 12 support; Ubuntu 22.04 and the RTX 4090 were not available for testing.

**G-3 (F-03)** README.md line 82, last sentence:

> A run on the grading machine uses its own engine, so expect its output to differ slightly from `results.jsonl.gz`. A rebuild on the same GPU model changed 0.12% of seconds; a different GPU (the RTX 4090) may differ by a different amount, which hasn't been measured.

The same idea applies to APPROACH.md line 297: "…will differ from `results.jsonl.gz`; on the same GPU model a rebuild changed 0.12% of seconds."

**G-4 (F-05)** README.md line 37:

> - The run makes no network calls of its own: `run.py` sets `YOLO_OFFLINE=1` and turns off Ultralytics' auto-install. With Python networking blocked (`validation/offline_guard.py`), the run made 0 network attempts.

**G-5 (F-06)** README.md line 54, replacement paragraph:

> If a file or video can't be read, decoding stops partway through, or the GPU runs out of memory on a single frame, the run carries on. For a video, it writes an `{"video": ..., "error": ...}` line after the lines already written. After a decode failure, every second decoded so far is still processed, including the unfinished last one (`--drop-partial-second` drops that one). After a failure during inference, seconds that were decoded but not yet written are lost. A Parquet file that can't be opened is reported as a `WARNING` on stderr; if its rows can't be read, each unread row gets an error line.

- `WRITEUP.md` was not audited (brief §8), and it doesn't exist yet.
- `validation/` contains no other Markdown files.
- No documentation, code, logs or git history were changed during this pass.

**Evidence used:**
- **Code, read statically:** `run.py`, `prep.py`, `requirements.txt` and the `validation/` tools.
- **Ultralytics 8.4.215 source** in the server's venv.
- **Raw logs** on the development server (`~/alethia/work/*/`): every `DONE` line, `/usr/bin/time -v` output, `profile/p0.json`, `sampling/sim.json` and `cleantest/pip_attempt3.log`.

- **Checks re-run for this audit, all CPU-only:**
  - `validation/test_run_unit.py`: 23 of 23 pass;
  - `validation/check_full_results.py` on the frozen results for files 00000 and 00001: `COMPLETE=True`;
  - set-disjointness checks on the subset manifests;
  - `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()`;
  - `free -b` and `lscpu`.
- **Not re-run:** no GPU job, dataset run, download or engine build was performed.

**Status key:**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| VERIFIED | Directly supported by executable code and/or reproducible evidence. |
| PARTIALLY VERIFIED | Supported only under stated conditions. |
| INACCURATE | Contradicted by the implementation or evidence. |
| OUTDATED | Was true historically but no longer describes the current version. |
| UNVERIFIABLE | The available evidence is insufficient to establish it. |

## A. Executive summary

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Substantive claims checked (register in section H) | **112** |
| VERIFIED | **84** |
| PARTIALLY VERIFIED | **16** |
| INACCURATE | **6** |
| OUTDATED | **4** |
| UNVERIFIABLE | **2** |

**Overall assessment:** the documentation is reliable on what the code does and on the measured numbers.

- **Implementation:** the sampling rule, aggregation, timestamps, model settings, fallback, OOM handling and threading all match the code exactly.
- **Measurements:** every wall time, frame count and accuracy figure checked against a raw log or result file matches, and every speed-up ratio recalculates correctly.

**The problems are of three kinds:**
1. **Deployment claims are stated more strongly than the evidence supports.**

2. **Memory figures use inconsistent units.** `/usr/bin/time` reports KiB, but the docs treat the values as kB and call the result GB.

**Evidence used:**
- **Code, read statically:** `run.py`, `prep.py`, `requirements.txt` and the `validation/` tools.

- **Raw logs** on the development server (`~/alethia/work/*/`): every `DONE` line, `/usr/bin/time -v` output, `profile/p0.json`, `sampling/sim.json` and `cleantest/pip_attempt3.log`.

| VERIFIED | Directly supported by executable code and/or reproducible evidence. |
| PARTIALLY VERIFIED | Supported only under stated conditions. |

| | Count |

**Overall assessment:** the documentation is reliable on what the code does and on the measured numbers.

- **Implementation:** the sampling rule, aggregation, timestamps, model settings, fallback, OOM handling and threading all match the code exactly.
- **Measurements:** every wall time, frame count and accuracy figure checked against a raw log or result file matches, and every speed-up ratio recalculates correctly.

**The problems are of three kinds:**
1. **Deployment claims are stated more strongly than the evidence supports.**
   - APPROACH.md describes the clean-environment test without saying that the final install was done with uv from a cache, not with pip.
   - Offline operation was tested only at the Python socket level.
   - Compatibility with the graders' driver and their RTX 4090 is an expectation, not something tested.
2. **Memory figures use inconsistent units.** `/usr/bin/time` reports KiB, but the docs treat the values as kB and call the result GB.
3. **Some details are left out or stale.** These include chunk size, queue accounting and error-path behaviour, plus stale statuses in DECISIONS.md.

There are **no Critical findings**, **1 High**, **5 Medium**, and the rest are Low.

content.text:
The documentation holds up well on implementation and on measured results. Its main weakness is deployment: it claims more than was actually tested. The full report is in [validation/DOCUMENTATION_AUDIT.md](validation/DOCUMENTATION_AUDIT.md). I haven't changed any documentation, code, logs or git history, and the report isn't committed.

**Totals:** 112 claims checked: 83 verified, 18 partially verified, 6 inaccurate, 3 outdated and 2 unverifiable. That produced 27 findings: no Critical, 1 High, 5 Medium and 21 Low.

**Checked against code and raw evidence, with nothing wrong found:**
- **Implementation:** the sampling rule (including that the neighbour comparison happens only after stage 1), aggregation, timestamps, rotation, model settings, letterbox, engine fallback, OOM handling and threading all match the code. I checked the decision logic itself, and the relevant Ultralytics source where it matters.
- **Timings:** every wall time and count matches its log. Recalculated: 3.65×, 5.82×, 7.18× and 12.36× (rounded to 12.4×) over the baseline, and −37.4%, −19% and −42.0% step by step.
- **Tests and data sets:** I re-ran the 23 unit tests and all pass; the fixture manifest has 17 entries; the dev, holdout and graded sets share no videos; the F1 calculations are correct.

**High and Medium findings:**
- **F-01 (High):** APPROACH.md presents the clean-environment test as a full deployment check. In fact pip never finished an install: it resolved every package, but this server's route to PyPI was too slow. The tested venv was installed with uv from its cache plus two hash-verified mirror wheels. A complete `pip install` on Ubuntu 22.04 has never been observed. D-027 records this correctly; APPROACH.md leaves it out.
- **F-02:** the README's "Tested with … an NVIDIA driver with CUDA 12 support" is true only for driver 595.99 on Ubuntu 26.04. Also, the torch build has no `sm_89` code, so the PyTorch fallback on the 4090 relies on its `sm_86` code; that's expected to work, but untested.
- **F-03:** both docs say the graders' output will differ from `results.jsonl.gz` "by about this much". That's a prediction from a rebuild on the same GPU model; nothing was measured on an RTX 4090.
- **F-04:** APPROACH.md's byte-identical claim for the original engine covers only the 66-video sequential set, not every set.
- **F-05:** "nothing needs the network" was tested only by blocking Python-level networking.
- **F-06:** the README's error-handling paragraph leaves out three things:
  - after a decode failure, the unfinished last second is still written;
  - after a failure during inference, up to 33 decoded but unwritten seconds are lost;
  - unreadable Parquet rows each get an error line.

**Low but systematic:**
- **Memory units:** `/usr/bin/time` reports KiB, but the docs treat the values as kB and call them GB. For example, "6.2 GB" is really 6.31 GB, or 5.87 GiB.
- **Other inaccuracies:**
  - RAM is 61.3 GiB, not the 62 GiB HARDWARE.md states;
  - chunks are 33 seconds, not 32;
  - the README's "F1 (macro gate)" label is wrong: the gate is min(micro, macro);
  - the fallback's accuracy is pointed to the wrong table.
- **Stale entries:** DECISIONS.md's index stops at D-025, and several statuses and to-do items are out of date.

**Can't be verified:** the "67 CPU-seconds" decode figure has no stored artifact, and nothing about the RTX 4090 or the graders' driver can be checked here.

Section G of the report has exact replacement wording for each finding. Shall I apply the corrections?

Under `validation/offline_guard.py`, which blocks Python networking, the run made 0 network attempts. - **Clean-environment test (D-027):** - Setup: a fresh venv and a fresh copy of the repository, then `prep.py`, then offline runs on dev and the holdout. - Scores with the newly built engine: dev F1 0.9918, people exact 0.9920, within ±1 0.9998; holdout 0.9935 / 0.9933 / 0.9999. The new engine changed 0.12% of seconds. With the original engine, the clean environment reproduced S-10 and `results.jsonl.gz` byte for byte, so the difference comes only from the rebuild. No `apt-get` packages are needed: PyAV ships its own FFmpeg, and OpenCV is the headless build. Tested with Python 3.11 and an NVIDIA driver with CUDA 12 support.
`requirements.txt` pulls about 9 GB of wheels. These include `tensorrt-cu12-libs` (4 GB) from NVIDIA's package index, listed at the top of the file, and the CUDA 12.6 builds of `torch` and `torchvision`, pinned as exact wheel URLs with sha256.
- Nothing needs the network: `run.py` sets `YOLO_OFFLINE=1` and turns off Ultralytics' auto-install.
- When the run finishes, a `DONE ...` summary line goes to stderr, with counts, the backend used and the wall time.
- If `weights/yolo11l.engine` is missing or fails to load, `run.py` prints a warning and carries on with PyTorch FP16. It's slower, but the results agree with the engine's to within the accuracy figures below.
If a file or video can't be read, decoding stops partway through, or the GPU runs out of memory on a single frame, the run carries on. For a video, it writes an `{"video": ..., "error": ...}` line and keeps the seconds it had finished. A Parquet file that can't be read at all is reported as a `WARNING` on stderr, and the run moves on to the next file.
| Decoding | PyAV, in a separate thread that overlaps with inference. A bounded queue of 512 MB of decoded frames sits between decoding and inference. | D-023 |
| Frame sampling | **Staged, `staged-1>3>all-VPN`**, described below the table. | D-016, D-017 |
| Model | YOLO11l as a TensorRT FP16 engine. Batches hold up to 32 frames of the same size, using Ultralytics' letterbox and NMS unchanged. | D-022, D-025 |
| Aggregation | An object is present if it is found in at least half of the frames run for that second. People is the floor of the median count over those frames. | D-015, D-017 |
| Memory | Decoded frames are bounded: chunks of 32 seconds or 1 GB, and a second larger than 512 MB streams straight through the model. On CUDA out-of-memory, the batch is halved and retried. | D-019 |
| Set | F1 (macro gate) | People exact | People within ±1 |
TensorRT doesn't build engines deterministically: each build may choose different kernels, which moves a few detections at the 0.4 confidence threshold. In a clean-environment test, a second engine built with `prep.py` changed 0.12% of seconds, and the dev F1 was 0.9918, with every metric still above the targets. Expect the same size of difference between `results.jsonl.gz` and a run on the grading machine (D-027).
| `tools/` | Helper scripts for syncing to the development server. |

The install and run steps above were tested on the development server, which is not the grading machine (D-027, D-029):

| Item | Tested |
|---|---|
| Machine | Quadro RTX 6000 (24 GB), Ubuntu 26.04, NVIDIA driver 595.99 |

| Install | `pip install --no-index --find-links wheelhouse -r requirements.txt`: the exact `requirements.txt`, installed by pip from a local cache of 69 files. That is the 67 pinned packages, plus `setuptools` and `wheel`, which pip needs to build the `tensorrt-cu12` source package. The install took 3 min 33 s, and `pip check` found no problems. |
| Cache contents | Every file's sha256 was checked against the hash published by PyPI (66 files) or NVIDIA's index (1), or pinned in `requirements.txt` (2), with `tools/verify_wheelhouse.py`. The files are identical to what `pip install -r requirements.txt` downloads. |
| Prep | `python prep.py`: 8 min 14 s, of which the engine build was 350 s. |
| Timed run | Offline, with Python networking blocked (`validation/offline_guard.py`): 0 network attempts. Dev F1 0.9918, people exact 0.9920, within ±1 0.9998; holdout 0.9935 / 0.9933 / 0.9999. All 17 fixtures and 23 unit tests passed. |
| Disk | about 8 GB of downloads and 14 GB for the installed venv, plus about 250 MB in `weights/` |

**Why the wheels came from a cache:** from this server, PyPI's file host and NVIDIA's index were often too slow (2–40 kB/s) for pip to finish downloading, and stalled downloads broke two attempts. - **Status:** Accepted: every check passes · **Date:** 2026-11-21
- **Context:**
  - D-027's install was completed with uv, not pip, because this server's downloads from PyPI were too slow.

  1. **Wheel cache:** `pip download --no-deps` for each line of `requirements.txt`, retried up to 5 times per package.
